paper_title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
caption: : Enhanced GCG task dependence. The effectiveness of Enhanced GCG varies widely across downstream tasks. Whereas this method nearly recovers the base model's accuracy for maximum letter probability generation, it offers little improvement in accuracy for maximum text generation tasks.

model_annotations.Chinese: This bar chart, titled "Evaluation Based on Different Tasks," visually compares the accuracy of three different models—labeled in the legend as "Base" (red), "RMU with Enhanced GCG" (light green), and "RMU" (light yellow)—across two distinct evaluation tasks: "MCQ Eval" and "Generation Eval." The vertical y-axis represents "Accuracy," scaled linearly from 0.0 to 0.6, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The horizontal x-axis presents the two evaluation tasks. For each task, the chart displays a stacked bar, where the total height represents the accuracy of the "Base" model, and the segments below it represent the contributions of "RMU with Enhanced GCG" and "RMU." Specifically, for "MCQ Eval," the red "Base" segment has a value of 0.644, the light green "RMU with Enhanced GCG" segment has a value of 0.539, and the light yellow "RMU" segment has a value of 0.299. For "Generation Eval," the red "Base" segment has a value of 0.597, the light green "RMU with Enhanced GCG" segment has a value of 0.263, and the light yellow "RMU" segment has a value of 0.106. The bars are arranged side-by-side along the x-axis, with no specific sorting order indicated, and all bars are visually presented with the same width and without any special emphasis such as shading or bolding.
